formulations.Polymer system Notes: Amorphous oxyethylene-oxymethylene random copolymer -[(CH2CH2O)n-CH2O-]m, n varies randomly around 9, m about 600; structurally similar to linear PEO. Doped with LiClO4 at O:Li = 64:1.
formulations.Polymer: amorphous PEO (oxyethylene-oxymethylene random copolymer, -[(CH2CH2O)n-CH2O-]m, n~9, m~600)
formulations.Notes: Conductivities are approximate values read off Fig. 5 (log10 conductivity vs Li:O ratio, 0.015 point ≈ 1/64). Fig. 4 Arrhenius plot readings for 64:1 do not agree well with these. Films were cast from ~3 wt% acetonitrile solution, the solvent was evaporated under dry argon, and the films were dried under vacuum and loaded in a dry box with 5 ppm H2O. dc conductivity was measured with a thick cell and blocking brass electrodes.
formulations.Reference: E. Linden, J.R. Owen, Conductivity measurements on amorphous PEO copolymers, Solid State Ionics 28-30 (1988) 994-1000

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Amorphous oxyethylene-oxymethylene random copolymer -[(CH2CH2O)n-CH2O-]m, n varies randomly around 9, m about 600; chain structure very similar to linear PEO with randomly spaced oxymethylene units. Doped with LiClO4 at Li:O = 1:24.
formulations.Polymer: amorphous PEO (oxyethylene-oxymethylene random copolymer, -[(CH2CH2O)n-CH2O-]m, n~9, m~600)
formulations.Notes: Li:O = 1:24 gives the highest conductivity. The paper attributes the drop at higher salt levels to a rising Tg and more ion pairing. The relaxation semicircle is much less depressed than for semicrystalline PEO. With Li electrodes a second semicircle appears, attributed to an interfacial impedance, possibly a reaction phase. Conductivities were read from Fig. 5 (dc values from thick-cell measurements).
formulations.Reference: E. Linden and J.R. Owen, Solid State Ionics 28-30 (1988) 994-1000

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Amorphous oxyethylene-oxymethylene random copolymer -[(CH2CH2O)n-CH2O-]m, n ~9 (random), m ~600; LiClO4 at Li:O = 1:16
formulations.Polymer: amorphous PEO (oxyethylene-oxymethylene random copolymer, -[(CH2CH2O)n-CH2O-]m, n~9, m~600)
formulations.Notes: Solvent evaporated under dry argon, then vacuum dried; cell loaded in a dry box (<5 ppm H2O). DC conductivity measured by impedance in a thick cell with brass blocking electrodes. Conductivity values are read from the Fig. 5 plot (Li:O ~0.06) of log conductivity vs dopant level, so they are approximate.
formulations.Reference: E. Linden and J.R. Owen, Conductivity measurements on amorphous PEO copolymers, Solid State Ionics 28-30 (1988) 994-1000

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Amorphous oxyethylene-oxymethylene random copolymer -[(CH2CH2O)n-CH2O-]m, n varies randomly around 9, m about 600; chain structure very similar to linear PEO. Doped with LiClO4 at O:Li = 12:1.
formulations.Polymer: amorphous PEO (oxyethylene-oxymethylene random copolymer, -[(CH2CH2O)n-CH2O-]m, n~9, m~600)
formulations.Notes: Solution about 3 wt% in acetonitrile; solvent evaporated under dry argon, then dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 24 h and loaded into the cell in a dry box (5 ppm H2O). The dc conductivity came from blocking-electrode impedance in a thick cell. Conductivity values were read off the plot in Fig. 5 (log σ vs Li:O ratio, 0.08 point about 1/12); they are approximate. The Fig. 4 Arrhenius plot readings differ by up to about 0.8 log units. Maximum conductivity was at Li:O = 1:24; it falls at higher concentrations, attributed to higher Tg and more ion pairing.
formulations.Reference: E. Linden and J.R. Owen, Solid State Ionics 28-30 (1988) 994-1000

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Amorphous oxyethylene-oxymethylene random copolymer -[(CH2CH2O)n-CH2O-]m, n varies randomly around 9, m about 600; structure very similar to linear PEO with randomly spaced oxymethylene units. Doped with LiClO4 at Li:O = 1:8.
formulations.Polymer: amorphous PEO (oxyethylene-oxymethylene random copolymer, -[(CH2CH2O)n-CH2O-]m, n~9, m~600)
formulations.Notes: Samples dissolved in acetonitrile (~3 wt% solutions) with LiClO4, solvent evaporated under dry argon, then dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 24 h and loaded in a 5 ppm H2O dry box. DC conductivity from thick-cell impedance with blocking brass electrodes. Conductivity values are plot readings from Fig. 5 (log10 σ vs dopant level). Fig. 4 Arrhenius-plot readings for 8:1 are about one decade higher, so those were not used. Conductivity falls above Li:O = 1:24, which the authors attribute to a higher Tg and more ion pairing.
formulations.Reference: E. Linden and J.R. Owen, Conductivity measurements on amorphous PEO copolymers, Solid State Ionics 28-30 (1988) 994-1000

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Semicrystalline linear high-molecular-mass PEO doped with LiClO4 at EO:Li = 8:1; used as a comparison to the amorphous oxyethylene-oxymethylene copolymer.
formulations.Notes: Only a corrected complex impedance spectrum from a thin cell is shown (Fig. 1c). Its relaxation semicircle is much more depressed than in the amorphous copolymer, which the authors attribute to microstructure. In PEO, the angle of depression decreased as temperature increased (experiments not reported in the paper). No conductivity values are given for this sample.
formulations.Reference: E. Linden, J.R. Owen, Conductivity measurements on amorphous PEO copolymers, Solid State Ionics 28-30 (1988) 994-1000
